articleTitle: Federated Learning Approach to Classification of DDoS Attacks by 2D-Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: This paper presents a federated learning approach to the classification of Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks using convolutional neural networks. The study employs the CIC-DDoS2019 dataset, which includes a variety of benign and malicious network traffic data. The classification task focuses on identifying specific types of DDoS attacks, such as Domain Name System (DNS), PORTMAP, and SYN Flood, alongside non-DDoS traffic. Utilizing MATLAB’s parallel server architecture, the research implements federated learning to train local models on distributed datasets, enhancing data privacy and security. The federated learning model achieves a global accuracy of 0.894 after 58 communication rounds (174 epochs), compared to a standalone training accuracy of 0.9607 after 300 epochs. While standalone training benefits from centralized data leading to higher accuracy, federated learning offers significant advantages in terms of scalability, privacy preservation, and utilization of decentralized computational resources.

articleTitle: Recognition and Classification of Direct Spread Spectrum Signals
abstract: This paper deals with the design and implementation of a direct spread spectrum signal classifier. The Binary-Phase Shift Keying (BPSK) and Quadrature Phase-Shift Keying (QPSK) modulation were used to create the signal patterns and Pseudo-Random (PR) sequences, Gold codes and Kasami codes were used to directly spread the spectrum of the modulated signals. The properties of the proposed direct spread spectrum signal models were simulated for Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) from 0 to 10 dB for different spread factor to make their properties close to real direct spread spectrum signals. The Welch’s power spectral density estimation method, wavelet transform and signal autocorrelation detection method were used for conceptual design and implementation of the direct spread spectrum signal classifier in Matlab programming environment.

articleTitle: The Effect of Mechanical Stress on the Sensitivity of Fiberoptic Polarization Temperature Sensor
abstract: The article analyses enhancing the sensitivity of fiber-optic polarization sensors to temperature changes via additional longitudinal strain. This multifunctional sensor is suitable for application as a sensing element for security purposes and has many possible biomedical applications. The testing method consists of stretching the fiber on a proof tester where it is possible to get an exact setting of the operating force, and then applying a container of water at a different temperature. Changes were captured by a laser power meter and plotted into graphs describing several sets of measurements to keep independence on manufacturing. The sensor sensitivity was increased and the proposed solution appeared to be suitable for in-position sensors with minimum additional outlays.

articleTitle: Improving GPS Reliability in Emergency Vehicles: A Case Study on Interference Source Identification
abstract: This study examines the impact of non-intentional electromagnetic interference on the reliability of Global Positioning System (GPS) within emergency vehicles, particularly ambulances. GPS is crucial for navigation, coordination, and communication in emergency response scenarios. Interference from onboard electrical equipment poses significant challenges to GPS functionality. Using a spectral analyzer, the research focuses on the 1 - 2 GHz band, including GPS L1, L2, and L5 bands, to identify sources of interference. The results reveal that specific electronic systems within the vehicles emit interference at levels sufficient to degrade GPS performance. The findings emphasize the need for a comprehensive analysis of Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) standards and highlight the importance of addressing these interference issues to ensure reliable GPS functionality. This measurement observation contributes to enhancing GPS reliability in emergency response operations, ultimately improving public safety and operational efficiency.

articleTitle: A Contribution to the Prevailing Visibility Prediction Based on Neural Network Approach
abstract: This paper explores visibility prediction from images through the integration of object detection and machine learning. The proposed approach utilizes the You Only Look Once (YOLO) neural network to detect and classify objects within images, which are subsequently used for visibility prediction using a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP). The aim is to propose an innovative approach for visibility prediction based on visual data and highlight YOLO’s performance in static scenarios. The work compares the neural network approach with a simple method that only identifies the furthest objects. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of YOLOv7 in this specific use case. Furthermore, it discusses potential improvements and approaches to enhance visibility prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: In-situ Imaging for Temperature Estimation in Laser Directed Energy Deposition with Wire Feedstock Using a Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: Accurate temperature estimation is crucial in metal additive manufacturing ensuring component quality and process efficiency. This study introduces the use of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), namely MobileNet and ResNet, to predict temperatures directly from melt pool images without the need for extensive preprocessing. Through comparative analysis, MobileNet demonstrated superior performance over ResNet, achieving a mean absolute error of 0.0562 and a correlation coefficient of 0.9900. These findings underscore the effectiveness of CNNs in real-time temperature prediction tasks within Laser-Directed Energy Deposition with wire (DED-LB/w), highlighting significant advancements and setting the stage for further technological enhancements.

articleTitle: Cyber Security Glossary-The Next Step
abstract: The main goal of the article is to bring comprehensive information about the Czech-Slovak Cyber security glossary, created and developed as an academic activity and a student work at the Department of Informatics and Cyber Operations of the University of Defense and the Department of Informatics of the Armed Forces Academy. The literature review presents more aspects of cyber security, analyzes its problems, offers cyber defense procedures, and mentions the implications for education and training. Almost all sources mention the issue of cyber security terminology in the form of a taxonomy or a dictionary. The software engineering system named ATOM (Aion Topic Maps engine) is the basis of the Glossary, its ontology and characteristics are mentioned, as well as the functions of a knowledge system. The relevance of the paper from the engineering point of view is in the structure and functions of the glossary. The Glossary version 3 is described in detail, the core Chapter suggests the next step Glossary version 4. The range of terms should be doubled, and the modified structure of the Glossary with the new class THEME will ensure better orientation in the vocabulary of the dictionary, see an example “Network”.

articleTitle: Radar Data Generation Algorithm at the Planar Phased Antenna Array Output
abstract: The paper presents the synthetic radar data generation algorithm of planar phased antenna array of the ground-based radar. The aim is clarified the method for radar data matrices generation received by the planar phased antenna array. Suitability of generated radar data matrices is verified by conventional beamformer technique. The generated radar data can be used for various methods e.g. Space-Time Adaptive Processing (STAP), beamforming methods or for radar signal processing artificial algorithms as a training or tested data. The paper consists of basic mathematical apparatus of received signals by the planar phased antenna array. The algorithm was formed in MATLAB and the theory takes into account the pulse without intrapulse modulation waveform and the planar antenna array of the ground-based radar.

articleTitle: A New Method for Polyphase Coded Radar Signals Recognition Based on Dual Channel Deep Learning
abstract: This paper presents a new method for recognizing polyphase coded radar signals based on dual-channel deep learning. The proposed method includes two stages. In the first step, the Morse Wavelet and continuous Wavelet transforms are used to extract signal features in the time and time-frequency domain. In the second, dual-channel deep learning is designed to recognize radar signals. The first channel uses the extracted feature in the time-frequency domain, and the second uses the phase change of the signals in the time domain. The proposed method’s performance is evaluated with simulated signals in a MATLAB environment. The simulation results approved that the proposed method provides a higher accuracy recognition than other methods, which only use single-channel deep learning with signal feature extraction in the time-frequency domain.

articleTitle: Use of Fractional-Order Lead Compensators to Increase the Robustness of Aircraft Control Systems
abstract: This paper deals with the use of the fractional-order calculus for the control of non-linear and non-stationary systems, such as aerodynamic systems. In the introduction, the paper raises the necessity for control of non-linear and nonstationary systems. Lead compensators are then introduced, first Integer-Order Lead Compensator (IOLC) and then Fractional-Order Lead Compensator (FOLC). An analysis of the effect of the various parameters of the FOLC on its frequency response is presented. Furthermore, the paper proposes to utilize these parameters to tune the FOLC using the Nyquist stability criterion. This proposal is finally demonstrated using an example of an FOLC tuning by an experimental method.

articleTitle: A Variant of the Larmor Frequency Calculation
abstract: The Larmor frequency is a basic parameter in the design and calculation of elements, especially in microwave technology. Its value is usually derived using moments, but this calculation is both laborious and lengthy and does not lead to the correct result for ferrites. The article describes a more elementary procedure for finding the Larmor frequency based not on moments, but on the equality of force action. The latter is much shorter, clearer, and simpler, and it also gives a result that is in agreement with the experimentally verified quantum theory.

articleTitle: Scalarization of Multi-Function Sensor Scheduling Problem
abstract: The VERA-NG system is a multifunctional passive surveillance system that simultaneously fulfills several functions. Concerning the hardware resources, it must solve the problem of scheduling the tasks of individual functions. This problem is defined as a multiobjective optimization. This work aims to solve this problem with the goal programming scalarization technique. Using a simple simulation, we demonstrate the properties of this approach and summarize its advantages over other scalarization techniques.

articleTitle: Radar Waveforms Based on Costas and Walsh-Hadamard Codes in Active Noise Jamming
abstract: The resilience of radar against active noise jamming techniques while maintaining the required probability of correct range estimation represents key factors for evaluating various radar waveforms. The given approach is carried out within electronics counter-countermeasures. This paper analyzes chosen combinations of frequency and phase intrapulse modulations and compares their performance under active noise jamming techniques while considering the required probability of correct range estimation. Based on the presented results, it is highly appropriate to use multiple frequency intrapulse modulations when active noise jamming techniques are present. To maintain the required probability of correct range estimation, a correlation receiver should be employed as well. Overall, using multiple-frequency intrapulse modulations (utilizing Costas codes) improved radar resilience against active noise jamming techniques.

articleTitle: Development of Malware Using Large Language Models
abstract: With the constant evolution of technology and military warfighting strategies, we are entering an era where traditional methods of exercise and simulation are being met with a new challenge - hybrid threats. With rapid advances in artificial intelligence and computer programming, new opportunities are also emerging in the realm of cyber threats. One of the latest developments is the ability of large language models to generate sophisticated and potentially malicious software. This new phenomenon opens the door for attackers to revolutionise approaches to hybrid threats. In this paper, we look at the challenges and opportunities associated with this issue and assess its potential implications for cybersecurity. The main goal is to verify if we can force ChatGPT representing Large Language Model (LLM) to create malware which will be then spreaded into exercising units.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Joint Gap Width Classification and Tack Weld Detection in Laser Beam Welding
abstract: Laser Beam Welding (LBW) requires precise control to ensure high-quality welds. Accurate classification of joint gap widths and detection of tack welds are crucial for optimizing the process and enhancing product reliability. This study investigates the application of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) to classify instant joint gap widths and detect the presence of tack welds during welding. The goal is to facilitate adaptive joint gap bridging in robotized and autogenous butt joint welding. Sequences of images resembling a time series were captured during welding of prepared workpieces with varying joint gap widths along the joint line. The results demonstrate that CNNs significantly outperform RNNs, achieving over 99 percent classification accuracy in both validation and test datasets, and 96 percent accuracy under conditions of substantial noise. These findings underscore the potential of CNNs in enhancing the precision and adaptability of welding automation. However, challenges remain in generalizing the CNN model to diverse and noisy operational environments.

articleTitle: The PCA and 1D-CNN Dimension Reduction Comparison for Hyperspectral Classification of Tree Species
abstract: This paper is focused on the comparison of two feature space dimensionality reduction approaches, namely Principal Component Analysis and One-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network to identify the hyperspectral classification model with the highest classification accuracy. The reference model is an enhanced multilayer perceptron without using dimension reduction. It differs from the standard multilayer perceptron by adding dropout layers, which prevent overfitting and stabilize the training process. The main idea of choosing a One-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network approach was to leverage its capability to reduce the feature space of the input data using a form of supervised learning. This way, it was possible to extract class-relevant features of the input data at a pixel level. The results show that the kappa score and the accuracy of the proposed model were 0.828 and 0.803 without dimension reduction, 0.863 and 0.843 with Principal Component Analysis, and for One-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network 0.847 and 0.825, respectively.

articleTitle: Signal Processing from Sensors and Data Processing Using a Probability Model
abstract: The article is focused on the practical implementation of signal processing during the transmission of coded messages through a laser system in distance measurement and data transmission using new progressive technologies and complex processing of information from sources and sensors using a probabilistic model. The aim of the work was the experimental verification of signal processing during distance measurement using the method of signal processing with the help of a probabilistic model and a standardized entropy estimation process after digitization of the received signals. The article describes the previously presented method of processing signals using a probabilistic model and its application in processing signals from sensors on the battlefield in determining the location of enemy targets and their identification using the recognition system – Identification Friendly or Foe (IFF) for Command, Control, Communications, Computers Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (C4ISR) systems. For the experiment, a laser module was designed to ensure the transmission of coded messages through a system with a laser signal detector to ensure data transmission and IFF recognition. The processing of signals during distance measurement was experimentally verified using the method of processing signals with the help of a probabilistic model and a standardized process of entropy estimation after digitization of the received signals. The application of laser modules to broadcast data in a laser communication channel expands the communication capabilities of a soldier or unit and to transmit information in tactical training systems and live simulation training systems.

articleTitle: Photopolymer Quality Measurement for SLA 3D Printing Using EIS
abstract: Additive Manufacturing (AM), and particularly 3D printing, plays a pivotal role in various domains of prototype and functional part production. This paper concentrates on photopolymers as the foundational material utilized in 3D printing via StereoLithogrAphy (SLA). A prevalent issue within AM is ensuring the base material achieves the correct form and possesses the desired properties. Photopolymers, primarily composed of oligomers, monomers, and photoinitiators, can exhibit drastically altered properties of the resin and consequently, the final printed material depending on the quantity and type of constituents used. Furthermore, the base material is subject to aging, which detrimentally impacts its properties and may ultimately result in defective prints. By assessing the electrochemical properties of the base material through Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS), it is feasible to measure and appraise these alterations. The analysis of three samples at varying stages of degradation reveals that the evaporation of the photoinitiator within the resin leads to the deterioration of the photopolymer. This degradation increases the likelihood of print failure, poses a heightened risk of incomplete polymerization, and enhances the potential for material delamination. Given the non-destructive characteristic of the EIS technique and the observable variances in the data, EIS can be affirmed as an effective method for monitoring the quality of resin.

articleTitle: Secure Communication Planning in LoRaWAN Network
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) networks keep scaling rapidly, introducing throughput bottlenecks. This paper proposes a novel communication planning approach for Low-Power Wide-Area Networks (LPWANs) to enhance energy and communication efficiency. By leveraging the Long Range Wide Area Network (LoRaWAN) protocol and the Network Server Slot-Based Communication Planning Protocol (NS-SCPP), we propose the infrastructure to carry out wireless communication over long distances with low energy consumption and more efficient communication. In IoT networks with many communicating devices, simultaneous transmissions may cause collisions. Collisions corrupt the transmitted data, leading to increased energy consumption and inefficient bandwidth and duty cycle utilization. In this paper, we propose a new medium access approach in the form of a protocol operating at the application layer. The protocol manages the communication schedule of end devices on the Application Server. The solution is supplemented by an additional security layer - the Certification Authority to ensure end device identity and message integrity.

articleTitle: Tactical Wireless Network Management Challenges in Urban and Suburban Areas: Analysis of Coverage Ranges
abstract: In this paper we discuss the problem of the planning of the tactical wireless networks in urban and suburban areas. The analysis is based on simulation results that cover communication backbone and wireless sensors deployed in areas with various urbanization scale. Different frequency bands that reflect the capability of currently used tactical radios were selected. They cover VHF, UHF and microwave bands. We also considered wireless sensor network deployment in urban areas. Wireless sensors technologies based on LoRa and Wi-Fi were modelled and coverages were assessed. In particular, we analyzed the possible benefit resulting from the frequency band change, the transmitter power increase and antenna height.

articleTitle: Review of Intrusion Detection Systems Taxonomy, Techniques, Methods and Future Research Directions
abstract: In the field of intrusion detection, research has made enormous progress over the past decade, and there are many articles devoted to this issue. Currently, however, intrusion detection covers a very wide spectrum of new technologies, and mapping this area, current trends and open problems could greatly help researchers find their way and choose the path to take. There are also many different reviews and studies in this domain, which provide different taxonomy and categorization for the same terms what is causing confusion, especially for new researchers in this domain. The article is providing comprehensive overview of different Intrusion Detection System (IDS) methodologies, techniques and taxonomy. Also, the most important principles are described so that the reader, after reading it, clearly understands what IDS is and what its different categories are, how it works. A big emphasis is placed on various open problems for future research.

articleTitle: Machine Learning and Transformers for Malware Analysis: Overview
abstract: Malware analysis and detection is a field of cybersecurity, which focuses on classification if a sample has malicious behavior and if it can damage or compromise information technologies or users. Since the creation of the first malware sample defenders have tried to come up with new approaches to detect malicious code and how to analyze it to extract more information about its purpose and its creators. Malware developers also need to refine their techniques to make analysis and detection harder so the result is constant competition between attackers and defenders. In recent years artificial intelligence has become part of malware analysis and detection and has promising results. Transformer models are part of a bigger group called large language models and their application to malware analysis and classification is still at the very beginning but few very recent studies have shown promising results. In this paper, we have first described the basics of malware analysis and its problems like evasive malware and obfuscation. Next, we have looked into basic machine learning techniques and how are they applied in malware analysis. Then we have analyzed the most recent and influential studies about the application of transformer models in this field. Contribution of this paper is in summarizing all identified problems that need to be solved in future work and outlining existing solutions that can be employed for malware classification.

articleTitle: Advanced Industrial Espionage: Mobile Device as Anti-Forensic and Anonymization Tool
abstract: This study explores the potential of resolving the issue of the industrial espionage with a commercial mobile device. In case of detection, forensic analysis and reverse techniques in the mobile device can be used to find out what videos, audio tracks and photos were made and sent. The work proposes a possible model in which the configurations of digital devices, the programmed application, and the behavior of entities in which each has a role are described. The result is a model designed and implemented by the author, which ensures safe and anonymous transmission of the created multimedia records sent to the decision-making entity. At the same time, the model makes it impossible to find evidence using forensic analysis and reverse engineering on the client and server side. It also considers and implements zero trust principles between entities in the proposed solution, thereby supporting personal security. The proposed model was demonstrated on creating and sending videos. It was proven by forensic evidence that the proposed model meets the established criteria.

articleTitle: Finding Initial Estimates of Impedance Model of Li-Ion Battery via Interactive Analysis
abstract: This paper describes a method for determining the initial values of the parameters of the impedance model of Li-Ion battery. The initial parameters are important for subsequent fitting the model to experimental data. The method is based on interactive analysis of impedance circuits, where the corresponding software tool automatically updates the circuit solution in the frequency domain after user’s modification of the circuit. It is thus possible to immediately evaluate the effect of this change on the impedance characteristic of the battery and to make these changes in a targeted manner to achieve a good match between the model and the measured characteristics. It is shown on the example of a SPICE-like simulation program that a good parameter estimation can be achieved in this way even without using standard least-square-method fitting tools.

articleTitle: Generating and Testing Binary Random Sequences for Classified Information Protection Systems
abstract: Binary random sequences are the basic material used to produce cryptographic keys, which are an essential factor guaranteeing the security of cryptographic algorithms and protocols used for information protection. We expect that discrete elements in a random sequence are uniformly distributed - the probability of appearing each of them is the same. In addition, random processes resulting in these sequences should be unpredictable. Binary random sequences can be obtained from hardware sources of randomness with proven stochastic properties. Truly random sequences produced by hardware random number generators are mainly used in cryptographic key management systems operating for the protection of classified information. This paper presents solutions for generating and testing truly random sequences.

articleTitle: Testing Accelerometers on Centrifuge Using Rate Table AC1120Si and Temperature Chamber
abstract: This article deals with accelerometers, one of the main components of Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs). Accelerometers in inertial measurement units are used together with gyroscopes, magnetometers, but also barometric and temperature sensors. Depending on their operating principle, accelerometers can be described using various mathematical models that define their basic parameters determining their transfer functions. In this article, a theoretical analysis of the use of the four-position and multi-position tests for testing accelerometers is performed. Next, the article deals with selected mathematical models of accelerometers, the design of an experiment for testing the ADXL326 accelerometer on a centrifuge, where rate table AC1120Si with temperature chamber VT7004) are used. The article proposes an experiment for testing the accelerometer in the entire dynamic range with the calculation of its basic parameters such as accelerometer offset, scale factor, determining the asymmetry of the transfer function and others. The main contribution of the article is the preparation of an experiment for testing an accelerometer using centrifugal acceleration, a mathematical description of the calculation of the parameters of the ADXL326 accelerometer model, and an evaluation of the contribution of individual methods of testing accelerometers.

articleTitle: Countermeasures Management in Cyber Defense Exercises
abstract: Current challenges in all kinds of computer systems add to the importance of adequately managing blue team tactics, techniques and procedures. Microsoft (MS) Windows operating systems together with the Active Directory domain environment are a crucial part of cyber-defense strategies of military or civil infrastructures. This fact is supported by cyber defense exercises, where these topics are covered in several scenarios. The main aim of this paper is to analyze the MS Windows cyber defense scenarios environment and the respective activities of the blue teams. Based on the analysis, this paper proposes an innovative solution for managing blue team tactics to detect misconfigurations and vulnerabilities in MS Windows. A ready-to-use automated tool provides a way for automated audit of security measures in the MS Windows operating system.

articleTitle: Methodology of Bivalent Data Management in Oracle Database
abstract: Relational databases are widespread, based on the entities and relationships forming the data model. Data to be handled can originate from various sources, delimited by the precision and format. The boolean data type is not part of the Structured Query Language (SQL) standard, resulting in the necessity to define the management on your own. Domain integrity is typically enhanced by the check constraint on the data model level or by trigger forming additional database object. This paper deals with the existing approaches emulating boolean data type in Oracle Database, but also focuses on mapping and specific boolean data type introduced in Oracle Database 23c. It aims to provide a methodology and performance study for using and modeling bivalent or trivalent values.

articleTitle: Security of Military Transmision in Public Mobile Radio Communication Systems
abstract: The technological changes occurring in 21st-century conflict theatres due to the use of drones and artificial intelligence have placed significant demands on the provision of continuous, secure and covert communications across the various battlefields. This article outlines potential opportunities to also leverage the civilian communications environment to provide non-survivable connectivity for the purpose of conducting military operations. By analysing the potential threats and pillars for the secure use of 5G mobile communications, it is possible to identify a series of possible solutions for incorporating this type of communication into the operational procedures of the Armed Forces of the Slovak Republic.

articleTitle: Artaban: Adaptive Control for Multidirectional Locomotion
abstract: This paper introduces Artaban, a quadruped robot designed for hazardous task execution and surveillance in perilous environments. Artaban’s unique leg design integrates cardan and four-bar mechanisms, resulting in intricate kinematics. Our study begins with an examination of the forward and inverse kinematics of Artaban’s legs, followed by the generation of Jacobians for each leg. By employing a Proportional-Derivative (PD) controller, we execute fundamental leg movements. We then delve into the inverse dynamics of the robot and its adaptive control using the Quad Software Development Kit (SDK) library. Through comprehensive simulations and hardware tests, we validate Artaban’s proficiency in executing various step types and movements, while also assessing its resilience to unexpected disturbances and ability to maintain balance.
